question: The clinical question is shared but the channel is not. Both papers include prediction of MCI-to-AD conversion in memory-clinic MCI: P-988 has 65 MCI patients (Bahia Blanca, about 40 months) and P-991 has 76 (Vienna, 12-48 months). P-988's predictor is eye movement recorded during the VSTMB memory-binding task (fixation duration, saccade amplitude), which is the eye channel. P-991's predictors are paper-and-pencil scores (MMSE, Sunderland CDT, VVT 3.0), which are the clinical/cognitive channel. Neither paper evaluates the other's instrument, and P-988 reports no prognostic analysis of its own MMSE or ACE-R scores.
metric: AUC in both: P-988 an in-sample ROC on groups defined at follow-up; P-991 a ROC within its MCI group.

figures.P-988: AUC 0.95 (sens 95%, spec 95%) for stable MCI vs MCI_C. MCI_C = 34; stable MCI is about 13, inferred as 65 - 34 - 18 converters to other pathologies. AUC 1.0 for MCI_C vs MCI_O. The prediction model was right for 34 of its 36 predicted converters, and none of its 29 predicted non-converters progressed to ADS, so accuracy against all non-converters is 63/65 = 0.969. No CI printed. Hanley-McNeil for 0.95 with n1 = 34, n2 = 13: Q1 = 0.95/1.05 = 0.9048; Q2 = 2(0.9025)/1.95 = 0.9256; SE = sqrt([0.0475 + 33(0.0023) + 12(0.0231)]/442) = 0.0301; CI [0.891, 1.000].

matched_figure_check: No matched figure exists. Neither paper reports the other's instrument, so nothing is reported under the other's condition. On the arithmetic alone, P-988's 0.95 sits just inside the MMSE interval (upper bound 0.952), while the MMSE's 0.808 lies outside P-988's interval [0.891, 1.000]. Against the MMSE the gap therefore exceeds uncertainty in one direction only; against the CDT and VVT it exceeds it in both. Every one of these comparisons crosses channels, which condition 1 does not allow.
performance_validity: On the PDF, P-988 meets the Section 3.5 exclusion in substance. Its prognostic figures are AUC 1.0 (MCI_C vs MCI_O) and 63/65 = 0.969 correct against all non-converters. Both are in-sample in 65 patients at one site, on groups defined at follow-up, with no external cohort and no confidence intervals, and the article text does not specify the prediction model. The 0.95 figure for MCI_C vs stable MCI is just below the threshold but comes from the same in-sample analysis. P-991 does not meet the exclusion: its prognostic AUCs are at most 0.808, and its 0.972 is an AD-vs-rest diagnostic figure.
reason: Both papers include MCI-to-AD prognosis in memory-clinic MCI and report AUC, but the channels differ. P-988 predicts from eye movements during a memory-binding task, P-991 from paper-and-pencil test scores, and neither evaluates the other's instrument, so condition 1 fails. P-988's prognostic results also meet the near-ceiling exclusion in substance: AUC 1.0 and 63 of 65 correct, in-sample, in 65 patients at one site, with no external cohort. On the question the record poses, whether a brief clinic test can carry prognostic signal, the papers agree, since P-991's MMSE reached AUC 0.808 within MCI.

quotes.quote: Data from baseline assessment and blind to clinical decisions entered such a model to predict who among those with MCI would more likely progress to ADS and who would not.
The analysis revealed that our eye-tracking metrics achieved 95% sensitivity and 95% specificity to distinguish between MCI and MCI_C patients (area under the curve [AUC] = 0.95).
Finally, when distinguishing between MCI_C and MCI_O, the sensitivity was 100% and the specificity was 100% (AUC = 1) (see Figure 4).

Of the 29 patients that the model predicted would not progress to ADS, 5 developed frontotemporal dementia, 2 developed Parkinson disease, 4 developed vascular dementia, 7 had major depression, and 11 remained as MCI.
A ROC curve was calculated for the original MCI group (n= 76). Progression was set as positive condition.
The MMSE showed an AUC of 0.808 (proposed cut-off 27.5, sensitivity 78.6%, specificity 71.0%, YI= 0.495, LR+= 2.72, LR–= 0.30, PPV= 0.38, NPV= 0.94).
The CDT had an AUC of 0.497, the VVT 3.0 Screening had an AUC of 0.488 so no further parameters were calculated.
None of the tests can be recommended to reliably predict disease-progress, solely the MMSE showed some validity in this task.
